policy: Manual visual classification of all67 dated tags from final-review-1.png, final-review-2.png, final-review-3.png and cutout-review.png; borderline outlines were checked in the full-size transparent cutouts. Categories describe the photographed main-body silhouette, not subject matter, theme icons or engraved designs. Ignore internal holes and small hanging rings, lugs or handle attachments. Circle retains small uniform rim serrations; oval means a visibly elongated continuously curved body; rectangle permits rounded corners and modest shoulder/end variation while retaining long straight opposite edges; shield means a badge-like body with shoulders and a tapering lower tip; triangle permits small clipped base corners; polygon covers distinctly angular multi-sided/tapered bodies; irregular retains substantial gear/sunburst/horseshoe or ornate external lobes. No mixed-object grouping or insufficiently legible silhouette was found in these67 reviewed cutouts, so none required unclassified. These are editorial visual observations, not Smithsonian catalog shape fields. Source links identify the original museum objects. The remaining310 collection silhouettes were manually reviewed from collection-shape-review/shapes-1.png through shapes-6.png on5 October2026 using the same main-body definitions. All377 objects now have documented visual observations; collar-mounted object details use the visible main tag outline. Shapes describe appearance, not museum catalog metadata.
